steps: Unpack & check contents
Unpack onto a clean, soft, dry surface and check the parts list: fireplace, manual, remote and batteries, boxed smoked crushed glass, glass suction clamp, power cord, (4) leveling legs.

In the boxElectric fireplace, instruction manual, remote control and batteries, smoked crushed glass (boxed), glass suction clamp, power cord, leveling legs (QTY 4)
Tools (not included)Phillips screwdriver, stud finder, level, tape measure, electric drill, 1/4" wood drill bit
Glass components: handle with extreme caution. Keep plastic packaging and small parts away from young children.
Choose insert or recessed
Insert: into an existing wood-burning fireplace, with a shroud covering the remaining opening. Recessed: into a framed opening, and then it must be hardwired by a licensed electrician (NFPA 70).

Follow all national and local building and electrical codes.

  • Location not susceptible to moisture, away from drapes and furniture.
  • No gasoline or other flammable vapors and liquids stored or used near the heater.
  • Using the supplied power cord: plan where it will connect to an electrical box.
  • Recessed: must be hardwired; all work by a licensed electrician to local and national (NFPA 70) electrical codes.

Meets H.U.D. construction and safety standards for manufactured homes when installed according to the manual.
Prep for the method

Insert: confirm an electrical connection inside the opening, fit the supplied cord, remove the (5) top-edge and (2) per-side screws, discard the side nailing flanges, fit the shroud (Figure 2.4) with the supplied screws. Recessed: bend out the nailing flanges and set the hardwire location.
Nailing flanges (recessed)
Two factory-attached flanges per side. Fold out per Figure 2.5: one way leaves the framing flush with the fireplace, the other recesses it by 1/2". Secure to the framing.
Frame the rough opening
Frame to the Figure 2.1 A / B / C dimensions for the model, at least 36" from combustibles in front, holding Table 2.1 clearances (0" bottom, sides and back; 1" top).
Electrical connection

Remove the (4) electrical box cover screws, move the cable clamp to the side, top or rear (knock-out plate), make the cord or hardwired connection and refit the cover. Dedicated 15 Amp (or higher) breaker.
Mantel, hearth & finishing

Combustible wall projection up to 12" starting at the top finishing edge; wall projection, finishing material and combustible mantel combined cannot exceed 12". Combustible hearth unlimited up to the viewing-area bottom. Nothing inside the viewing area; the glass front must stay removable.
Glass off, media & logs
With the unit in its final position, remove the glass front, spread the supplied crushed media evenly over the whole floor, add an optional log set, and refit the glass.

1. Remove any exterior trim or Chaska screen hanging brackets first.
  2. One hand on the glass; remove the screws and brackets at the top right and left. Save them.
  3. Lift the glass away; lay it face down on a soft, non-abrasive surface.
  4. Crushed media: an even layer the full width and depth of the floor.
  5. Optional log set: (4) charred base logs in front of the pulsating ember bed LEDs, then the remaining logs (photos on the log set pages).
  6. Refit the glass with the two top clips and screws, and any other removed components.
Osseo e29: there is an air channel in front of the glass valance channel. Reinstall the glass in the channel it was removed from.
Surround or Chaska bracket

Recessed only, after media, logs and glass valance are in. Surround: align the inside flange with the opening; (4) screws into the (2) threaded fittings per side. Chaska bracket: screws into the inside side-edge fittings, then hang the screen in its slots.

Both cover the edge of the finishing material, and either must come off again to remove the glass.

  • Rectangle surround (OSE29-RS / OSE34-RS): covers an unfinished or exposed edge of finishing material (drywall or wood) that is flush with the appliance.
  • Chaska hanging bracket (OSE29-CHB / OSE34-CHB) with a Chaska screen barrier: covers finishing material up to 1" thick. Top position: the screen covers all 4 edges of the finishing material. Bottom position: the screen sits flush with the bottom of the appliance, for a hearth flush with the bottom.
Pair the remote & test

Turn the main switch on (standby), hold the two control-panel buttons marked in Figure 5.1 for 5 seconds, release, then press power on the remote. Power should now turn the unit on and off; if not, repeat.

on.title: Turning it on and setting the heat
on.html:
Your fireplace has a control panel on the unit, plus a remote. Each panel button beeps when you press it.

  1. Push the main power switch to I. The main power indicator lights up.
  2. Press the manual switch button to turn the fire on. Press it again to turn the fire off.
  3. For heat, press the heater button: once for half heat (750W), a second time for full heat (1500W), and a third time to turn the heater off.

The flame, down light and floor LED buttons change the look (see Flames, lights and sound). You can also use the remote, as long as the rocker switch on the control panel is on.

A slight odor the first time you turn it on is normal. It shouldn't come back unless the fireplace sits unused for a long time.

Turning it fully off

Turn the controls off, then switch off the power to the heater circuit at the main disconnect panel.

This heater gives extra (supplemental) heat only. It isn't meant to be your main heat source.

remote.title: Using the remote
remote.html:
The remote has its own set of features, including the thermostat and timer. The rocker switch on the fireplace's control panel must be on for it to work.

Waking it up

After 60 seconds without use, the remote goes into safe mode. Press the unlock button before you use it. The screen backlight comes on.

The main buttons

  • Power turns the fireplace on or off. If the remote hasn't been used in the last 60 seconds, press power once to unlock it, then a second time to turn the fireplace on or off.
  • Heater turns the heat on and off. One press gives half power (750W), a second press full power (1500W). An "Off" icon on the screen means the heater is off.
  • Up and down arrows change the temperature setting, or the brightness inside an effect.
  • SET saves a change. If you stop pressing buttons for 3 seconds, it saves on its own.

Handy extras

  • Hold SET for 6 seconds to switch the readout between Fahrenheit and Celsius.
  • To lock the remote, press the on/off button for 60 seconds until the lock icon shows. Hold it for another 60 seconds to unlock.

effects.title: Flames, lights and sound
effects.html:
You can change the look from the remote or from the control panel. On the remote, press an effect button and its icon flashes: that effect is now active.

From the remote

  • Flame: the up and down arrows set flame brightness, with 5 settings from full flame to no flame. The - and + buttons change the color, 1 to 4.
  • Down LED: up and down set the brightness, with 5 settings from maximum brightness to no light.
Note: p. 27 says the up and down arrows set the down LED's brightness in 5 settings, then says the - and + buttons "adjust the light brightness from number 1 to 7". On the control panel, the down light has seven colors (p. 24).
  • Floor LED: up and down set the brightness (5 settings). The - and + buttons change the color, 1 to 13.
  • Press an effect button a second time, and keep pressing, to cycle through its color options.
  • Ember bed: a red LED pulses like glowing embers. Hold the Floor LED button for 5 seconds to turn it on or off.
Maker's website: Ember Bed: 13 colors, 5 intensity levels. In the manual, those are the floor LED's figures.
  • Wood-crackling sound: the background sound button has four settings: low, medium, high and mute.

From the control panel

  • The flame button steps through four flame color and pattern settings.
  • The down light button has seven colors; the floor LED button has thirteen.
  • With the fireplace on, hold either of those for 3 seconds until it beeps to start a mode. Hold another 3 seconds for the next one: pulse (single color), pulse (color changing), solid state (color changing), solid state (single color).
Pick your color first, before you switch on a single-color mode.

thermostat.title: Thermostat and timer
thermostat.html:
The remote is also the thermostat. It reads the temperature where it sits.

Where to keep the remote

  • In the same room as the fireplace, with its screen facing up.
  • Don't cover its temperature sensor.
  • Not next to the front of the fireplace or somewhere warm like a window. It will read the wrong temperature, and the fireplace won't turn on and off accurately.

Setting a temperature

Press the up or down arrow to change the setting, then press SET or wait 3 seconds to save it. For example, set it to 70°F and the heater starts on its own when the room is at 66°F. It works to a +/- 3°F tolerance.

Timer

Press the timer button to cycle through times from 30 minutes to 8 hours. The timer controls the whole fireplace: when it reaches 0 minutes, everything shuts off.

Running it from the panel instead

Raise the set temperature above the room temperature, then turn the remote off. That stops the remote overriding the control panel. Note: if the main power switch is turned off and the fire is turned on manually again, the heat won't work.

clean.title: Cleaning the glass and vents
clean.html:
Turn the power off first: set the toggle switch on the control panel to off. The manual also says to always disconnect the heater from its power supply before any cleaning.

Vents and heater area

Keep the air inlet and heater area free of dust, lint and pet hair, and check the vents before each use.

Note: p. 7 says to unplug the appliance and clean the air vents with a vacuum only; p. 28 says to clean the air inlet and heater area with a cloth or vacuum.
  • Never rinse it or let it get wet, and don't spray liquids directly onto it.
  • Don't use abrasive cleaners.

The glass

Spray glass cleaner onto a cloth, wipe the glass, then dry it with a lint-free cloth.

A hard impact will shatter the glass, so take extra care that its corners don't hit anything hard. If you take the glass out to clean it:

  • Wear safety gloves and glasses.
  • Set it on a soft surface.
  • Don't carry it by the suction cups. They're only there to tilt the glass back so it can be removed.

batteries.title: Remote batteries, reset and pairing
batteries.html:
The remote takes (3) AAA batteries. Use the correct type, 1.5V AAA. Replace them when the battery indicator on the remote is empty, and put each one in the right way round.

After new batteries, set the clock

  1. Turn the remote on and hold the timer button for 5 seconds. The display goes blank except for the time.
  2. Press SET. The hour blinks; change it with the up and down arrows.
  3. Press SET to move to the minutes, adjust them, then press SET again.

If the remote isn't working right

Reset it to factory settings: open the back cover, take the batteries out, then put them back with the polarity correct.

Pairing the remote again

Turn on the main switch on the fireplace to put it in standby. Press and hold the two control-panel buttons marked in Figure 5.1 on p. 23 of the manual for 5 seconds, release, then press power on the remote. Test it: power should turn the fireplace on and off. If it doesn't, repeat the steps.

power.title: Outlets, cords and power
power.html:
This fireplace draws more current than other small heaters, so overheating can happen even where other heaters were fine. Treat the outlet with care.

  • Plug the power cord directly into a wall outlet. Never use an extension cord or a power strip.
  • Never use an outlet that is old or cracked, or has loose wires or connections. It could arc, overheat or catch fire.
  • Check that the plug fits tight. A loose plug or a faulty outlet connection can overheat the outlet.
Rating120VAC, 60Hz, 1500W
CircuitDedicated 15 Amp (or higher) breaker

In a recessed (built-in) installation, the manual requires the fireplace to be hardwired by a licensed electrician.

Turning the power off

To disconnect the heater, turn the controls off and switch off the heater circuit at the main disconnect panel. If it ever malfunctions, stop using it, disconnect the power at the service panel and have an authorized Kozy Heat dealer inspect it before you use it again.

safety.title: Safety around the heater
safety.html:
• The heater is hot when in use. Don't let bare skin touch hot surfaces.
  • Keep combustible materials, such as furniture, pillows, bedding, papers, clothes and curtains, at least 36" from the front.
  • Take extreme care when children or anyone needing extra care are near it, and whenever it's left running unattended.
  • Don't block the air intakes or exhaust, and don't let anything get into a vent or exhaust opening. That can cause an electric shock, a fire or damage.
  • It has hot and arcing or sparking parts inside. Don't use it where gasoline, paint, or flammable vapors or liquids are used or stored.
  • Don't use it outdoors, and don't rely on it as your main heat source. It's for supplemental heat only.
  • Don't tamper with any controls.
After a malfunction, don't run it again. Disconnect power at the service panel and have an authorized Kozy Heat dealer inspect it before reusing it.

Keep the plastic packaging and small parts from the box away from young children.

logs.title: Crushed glass and log sets
logs.html:
Your fireplace comes with smoked crushed glass for the firebox floor. A traditional log set (OSE-TLS) or birch log set (OSE-BLS) is optional.

Maker's website: Optional Media: Traditional log set, Birch log set, Real timber log set.

Getting to the media

  1. If a rectangle surround or Chaska screen hanging brackets are fitted, remove them first.
  2. With one hand on the glass so it can't fall, remove the screws and brackets at the top right and left. Keep them.
  3. Lift the glass away and lay it face down on a soft, non-abrasive surface.

Media and logs

  • The fireplace must be in its final position first. Spread the crushed media in an even layer over the full width and depth of the floor.
  • Both log sets start with (4) charred logs in front of the pulsating ember bed LEDs. In the birch set, the two larger logs go on the sides and two smaller birch logs in the center. The traditional set's two large side logs are semi-transparent so the flames glow through. The manual shows each layout in photos.

Refit the glass with the two top clips and screws. On the Osseo e29, put it back in the same glass valance channel it came out of.

warranty.title: Warranty at a glance
warranty.html:
Hussong Mfg. (Kozy Heat) warrants this electric fireplace to the original purchaser against defects in materials and workmanship at the time of manufacture.

Parts2 years
Labor reimbursement1 year, paid to an authorized dealer only
Note: the warranty page is headed "Limited Lifetime Warranty" on p. 31 (and in the contents on p. 5); the coverage text on p. 31 gives a "2 Year Limited Warranty", with parts for 2 years and labor for 1 year.
  • Coverage starts on the date of original purchase. In new home construction, it starts at first occupancy or six months after the dealer sale, whichever is earlier. The manual adds: "The warranty shall commence no later than 24 months of the occupancy date."
  • It covers only fireplaces bought through an authorized Kozy Heat dealer or distributor, and it can't be transferred.
  • No documents need to be sent in. Keep your proof of purchase with the date, serial number and model.
  • It must be installed by a licensed, authorized service technician or contractor, and installed, operated and maintained as the manual says, or the warranty is void.

Not covered

Wear parts (paint, batteries, glass discoloration), finish color changes, cleaner damage to plated surfaces, power interruptions or fluctuations, damp places such as outdoors, porches and laundry rooms, water or weather damage, service by a non-authorized provider without pre-authorization, and how well it heats your space.

No 3-slot receptacle: an adapter (not included) must be used, its green grounding lug connected to a permanent ground such as a properly grounded outlet box. Don't use the adapter if a three-slot grounded receptacle is available.

The cable clamp (secures cord or hardwiring) moves to the side, top or rear via the knock-out plate; the electrical box cover is held by (4) screws.

The unit ships so it can be hardwired or connected with the supplied power cord (p. 17). With the cord: always plug directly into a wall outlet/receptacle, never an extension cord or power strip (p. 7). Recessed installation: must be hardwired (p. 8, p. 10 and p. 17).

conflicts.issue: Page heading (and table of contents) says 'Limited Lifetime Warranty'; the coverage text on the same page is headed '2 Year Limited Warranty' and gives all parts 2 years, labor reimbursement 1 year.
Vent cleaning: safety list item 12 says 'Unplug the appliance and clean with a vacuum ONLY'; maintenance section says clean the air inlet and heater area 'with a cloth or vacuum'.
Safety list item 11 says 'ALWAYS plug the heater directly into a wall outlet/receptacle with the power cord'; sections 1.3, 2.1 and 2.9 say a recessed installation must be hardwired.
conflicts.reason: Section 2.9 (p. 17) says the unit ships to be either hardwired or connected with the supplied power cord, and requires hardwiring only for a recessed installation; item 11 (p. 7) is the rule for using the cord: directly into a wall outlet, never an extension cord or power strip. Both fit; the specElec drawer now states each for its case.

conflicts.issue: Remote down LED (p. 27): 'Press the up or down arrow to adjust the light brightness. There are 5 settings which range from maximum brightness or no light', then 'Use the - and + button to adjust the light brightness from number 1 to 7'. Two brightness scales for the same light; the flame and floor LED paragraphs use - and + for color, and the control panel's down light has seven color settings (p. 24).

review.notes: No troubleshooting chart and no code table in the manual: the three fault panels use only fault statements from the safety list (p. 7) and the operating and maintenance sections (pp. 23, 25-28); codes left empty. Lettered dimensions (Figure 1.1 p. 9, Figure 2.1 p. 14) are transcribed with the letters as printed; the text never says which letter is height, width or depth. Shown only in figures, so drawers point to them: the two pairing buttons (Figure 5.1 p. 23), the mantel/hearth projection zone (Figure 3.2 p. 19), nailing-flange orientation (Figure 2.5 p. 12), shroud fitting (Figure 2.4 p. 11), log layouts (pp. 21-22). Remote down LED (p. 27): up/down sets brightness in 5 settings, then '-'/'+' are said to 'adjust the light brightness from number 1 to 7' (flame and floor LED paragraphs use -/+ for color; the panel down light has seven colors, p. 24). Both brightness figures are shown in an amber note in the effects drawer and recorded in review.conflicts (Oct 12 spot-check). Remote lock 'press the on/off button for 60 seconds' (p. 25) transcribed as printed. p. 25 says press 'unlock' to wake the remote; p. 26 says press power once to unlock; both given. p. 28 calls the glass 'temperature for safety' (probably 'tempered'); the drawer avoids the word. The manual uses main power switch, rocker switch, toggle switch and main switch for the panel switch; each is kept as printed in its context. The manual gives no BTU figure, unit weight or viewing-area dimension, so catalog electric_btu_max, weight_lb and view_area can't be checked. The catalog's OSO-e34 website view_area (19-1/16" x 32-5/16") differs from its own brochure value (22-7/8" x 32-5/16"); in the manual 19-1/16" appears only as the OSO-e29's lettered dimension A (OSO-e34 A is 22-7/8", Figure 1.1). Catalog features mention real-timber log sets, Chaska shrouds and a reflective glass firebox liner; the manual lists only traditional (OSE-TLS) and birch (OSE-BLS) log sets, and its insert installation calls for 'a shroud' with no part number in the accessory list. Warranty start clause 'The warranty shall commence no later than 24 months of the occupancy date' (p. 31) is quoted as printed in the warranty drawer (Oct 12 spot-check). Pages 2, 4 and 6 are blank. Listing lab: Intertek Testing Services; the cover also states H.U.D. compliance for manufactured homes. Oct 12 update: website.json has no clearance row, so the specClear note, labelled 'Maker's brochure', quotes the brochure wording kept in the catalog's clearances_note; website notes also added for Power (5,000 BTUs, which the manual doesn't give), Ember Bed (13 colors / 5 levels, which the manual gives for the floor LED) and Optional Media (real timber log set, not in the manual).
